newsitem.title: INDIA: INTERVIEW-Indian stocks seen as Asia's best bet.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Indian stocks seen as Asia's best bet.

text.p: Expectations of an economic upturn and attractive valuations make Indian shares the best bet among Asia's emerging markets, the head of an international fund management firm said on Thursday.

"Both domestically as well as offshore, people had been looking at India as cheap and that makes a very compelling story," Nikhil Khattau, chief executive officer at SUN F&C Asset Management (I) Pvt Ltd told Reuters in an interview.
SUN F&C is the Indian affiliate of London-based Foreign & Colonial Emerging Markets Ltd. SUN F&C launched a domestic open-ended equity mutual fund on May 23.
It launched its $14 million offshore India Performance Fund in May 1996.
A steep 42 percent rally in the main Indian stock index since the close of 1996, largely led by foreign fund buying, has made Indian markets the best performers in Asia this year, analysts said.
In afternoon trade on Thursday, Bombay's benchmark 30-share index was down 22.20 points, or 0.51 percent, at 4,311.70, off the day's peak of 4,393.29 -- a 33-month high.
Loose monetary policy, falling interest rates and weaker local real estate and global bullion markets have been the keys to the attractiveness of Indian shares, Khattau said.
"We are beginning to see the results of a fairly loose monetary policy adopted over the last 18 months. Real interest rates are at a low."
"There is so much money awash in the system," Khattau said.
Indian interest rates have fallen sharply, triggered by cuts last week in major banks' prime lending rates to 13.5 percent -- the lowest in more than two years.
Since April 1, the central bank's key rate has dropped by two percentage points to 10 percent.

"If you take the medium and long term view, corporate profitability and growth should start picking up. Profit after tax growth should come back to 20-25 percent levels (in 1997/98 April-March) after falling significantly last year," Khattau said.
But half-year results are likely to remain under pressure from the effects of a slowing economy, Khattau said.
Despite the lack of any data indicating an economic upturn, he said the outlook for the Indian economy was favourable.

"All the elements are there. There is liquidity in the system, interest rates are at all time lows, inflation is not an issue at the moment .... the monsoon is showing signs of being a good one," he said.
